analysis:
This batch contains test-only changes, so no finding is reported from it. The tests do signal three production behavior changes that the integration pass must verify against their source.

1) GLM5ToolFailureTests.swift head 33-50: forced tool_choice (required or named) for glm5_next previously threw. It is now served by structuredPostValidation through the native GLM parser (format .glm5, !streamsCalls). The JSON parser is rejected for that strategy. Lines 82-87 check that invalid output from a withheld call commits no calls and leaks no visible text (relevant to T-008 and A-001 data exposure). They also check the mapping: 422 when forced, 500 under auto. Production sources (ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy, ToolStreamPreparation, MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine stream withholding) were not supplied. Integration must confirm that withholding cannot leak partial plaintext or an early tool call, and that the 1 MiB frame bound holds (line 29).

2) GLM5NextMediaRoutingTests.swift head 237-266: JSON response_format and forced tool_choice are refused together with media before any preparation; production enforcement must be verified. Head 290-342: variable-frame-rate QuickTime and mp4 clips are now accepted, where they were previously rejected as invalid_media. This widens the media-ingest surface (decode bounds, DoS, temp-file handling per T-050, reservation budgets). The MediaIngest changes need source review. The test fixture loader at lines 129-135 reads repo-local resources only.

3) GLM5NextProviderLoopTests.swift head 194-220: the model load now publishes its own verified SHA-256 digest with no WeightHasher re-read. The live registration hash equals the manifest aggregate, and a VerifiedWeightHashStore record is keyed by file identities. This affects T-012 and T-027 (weight substitution) and the T-041 weightHash binding. Integration must verify three things: the digest is computed over the bytes actually loaded (no TOCTOU between hashing and mmap or load); fileIdentities (inode, mtime, size?) cannot be spoofed by an operator to reuse a stale verified record after a weight swap; and the record file has owner-only permissions. No production source was supplied for these.
